items.q: What is the main thesis of the editorial?
items.a: That Palladio's method can be read as an early, well-documented system of explicit production rules, comparable to a curated dataset, but that the analogy with generative AI breaks down at licence: a deviation from the rule motivated by a circumstance and traceable to a judgement, never a statistical fluctuation without a cause.

items.q: Why does the title call Palladio "the first algorithm"?
items.a: Deliberately and provocatively. Palladio was neither the only nor the first to design with explicit rules (Vignola and later Durand were even more prescriptive). What makes his case exemplary is that rule, proportional system and motivated variation coexist in one corpus documented by treatise, drawings and buildings, which is why it became the testing ground of computational design research.

items.q: In what sense is the treatise like a dataset?
items.a: Palladio does not invent his rules: he extracts, selects and normalises them from a pre-existing corpus of ancient sources, surveys and precedents. As Wittkower and Carpo showed, the result is a selected version of antiquity, just as a training dataset is never a neutral sample of reality.

items.q: Where does the analogy between treatise and dataset stop working?
items.a: At two points. First, scale and authorship: a treatise is selected by an author who answers for it, while datasets such as LAION-5B aggregate billions of web-scraped pairs for which no one answers in full. Second, and decisively, variation: in Palladio a deviation has a declared cause; in a generative model it comes from stochastic sampling.

A shape grammar published by George Stiny and William J. Mitchell in 1978: a set of explicit, parametric rules that generates the plans of Palladian villas, starting from the Villa Malcontenta. It shifts the idea of style from a repertoire of forms to a system of transformations.

items.q: What are the historical corpus, the generative language and the design space?
items.a: Three nested levels: the buildings Palladio actually realised; the configurations the grammar admits (for example ten plans on a 3 × 3 grid and 220 on a 5 × 3 grid); and all configurations obtainable by combining the rules. The gap between what was built and what could be generated is where judgement operates.

items.q: Why is drawing described as an instrument of thought rather than a technique?
items.a: Following Alberti's lineamenta, Raphael's Letter to Leo X and Robin Evans, architectural drawing is measurable and verifiable, and it produces knowledge: its eidetic dimension makes an unformed thought visible, and its heuristic function reveals relationships the designer had not foreseen, within a hypothesis being tested.

items.q: What does recent research say about AI models and Palladian buildings?
items.a: A 2025 experiment asked GPT-4o and Claude 3.5 Sonnet to synthesise the Villa Rotonda and Palazzo Porto in 3D from the Quattro libri: both generated the parts but struggled to assemble them according to the required spatial relationships. What is missing is control over relationships, which is exactly what a grammar makes explicit.

items.q: What critical protocol does the editorial propose?
items.a: Five criteria for evaluating generative outputs: provenance (model, data, prompts, parameters, also required by the EU AI Act, Art. 50); rule; measure in plan, elevation and section; documented and motivated deviation; and explicit responsibility of an author for the final decision.

Students start from drawing rather than from the generated image: they survey, redraw and formalise the rules of a Palladian case, then use AI to produce variants to be verified against the protocol. What is assessed is the judgement dossier accompanying each variant, so AI becomes a sparring partner rather than a substitute.
